text: dsh-session-inbox 是一个面向 DSH 会话的文件收件箱插件，通过挂载到宿主并定期检查 JSONL 收件箱，在目标会话在线且空闲时把消息作为普通用户轮次交给 agent。它配套提供命令行工具，可投递消息、查看待处理数量并列出有收件箱的会话；消息会留在本地文件中，目标忙碌或不在线时等待之后处理。适合在本机进程之间向 DSH 会话排队发送文本。默认使用 ~/.dsh/inbox，可通过目录配置调整；不需要 API Key 或外部服务。

dsh-session-inbox is a file inbox for DSH sessions. It polls local JSONL files and delivers queued text as a normal user turn when the target session is idle. A companion CLI sends messages and lists pending inboxes. It uses ~/.dsh/inbox by default and needs no API key or external service.
想从本机脚本给空闲的 DSH 会话排队发送一条文本消息。
DSH 会话正在忙时，怎么先把消息存下来等它空闲后再接收？
I want to queue a text message for a DSH session and check how many messages are waiting.
dsh-session-inbox 的功能「会话消息收件箱」：命令行将带接收会话和正文的消息追加到 JSONL 文件；插件轮询收件箱，在目标会话空闲时将消息作为普通用户轮次交给 agent。

给 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 会话用的**收件箱**。

任何进程——另一个 DSH 会话、Claude Code、Codex、脚本、CI，或者你自己——往
`~/.dsh/inbox/<sessionId>.jsonl` 追加一行 JSON 即可。目标会话活着且空闲时，插件会把这条消息
取走，作为一条普通的用户消息交给该会话。

没有 socket、没有守护进程、没有握手、没有 MCP 服务。一条消息就是文件里的一行，所以目标被关闭、
被杀、被重启，消息都还在。

dsh-session-inbox README · 为什么需要它：各家 agent 内部早就能互相发消息：Codex 有 `queue`，Claude Code 有会话间消息，DSH 有 session
bridge。但**跨产品**没有共享的会话注册表、没有共享路由、也没有共享的 agent 循环，所以没有任何
东西能唤醒属于别人的会话。

文件系统是每个进程都能碰的唯一交集，于是交接发生在这里：**投递落到磁盘，执行留给会话的所有者。**

dsh-session-inbox README · 消息格式：一行一个 JSON 对象，行末必须有换行。`to` 必须等于文件名去掉 `.jsonl`。

```json
{"id":"<uuid>","ts":"<ISO-8601>","from":"<谁>","to":"<sessionId>","text":"<正文>"}
```

dsh-session-inbox README · 行为：| 情况 | 表现 |
| --- | --- |
| 目标活着且空闲 | 注入，游标前进 |
| 目标正在跑 | 留在文件里，不打断 |
| 目标不存在 | 一直保留，等该会话出现 |
| 坏行 | 永久跳过，避免堵住队列 |
| 多条消息 | 一次一轮，串行消费 |

游标在 `~/.dsh/inbox/.state/`，**只前进不后退**，所以第二个宿主不会把游标写回旧值、导致重放。

dsh-session-inbox README · 边界：- **推不进不属于你的会话。** 插件只服务挂载它的那个 DSH 宿主内的会话，够不到别的产品的会话。
- **`from` 是自报字段。** 任何能写收件箱的进程都能冒充任意发件人，**绝不能拿它做授权判断**。
- **投递不等于确认。** 入队成功不代表模型读到了；需要确认就约定「带 id、回显 id」。

dsh-session-inbox README · 兼容性：`engines.dsh` 是纯下限（`>=0.1.7-0`），不设上界。插件除了宿主注入的 `agents` 之外不 import 任何
DSH 包，所以不会钉死 harness 版本。

A **mailbox for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) sessions**.

dsh-session-inbox README · dsh-session-inbox：Any process — another DSH session, Claude Code, Codex, a script, a CI job, or you — can drop one
JSON line into `~/.dsh/inbox/<sessionId>.jsonl`. When that session is live and idle, this plugin
picks the message up and hands it to the agent as a normal user turn.

No socket, no daemon, no handshake, no MCP server. A message is a line in a file, so it survives
the target being closed, killed, or restarted.

dsh-session-inbox README · Why：Agents can already message their own kind: Codex has `queue`, Claude Code has session messaging,
DSH has its session bridge. Between *different* products there is no shared registry, no shared
router and no shared agent loop, so nothing can wake a session that belongs to someone else.

The file system is the one thing every process can touch, so it is where the hand-off happens:
delivery goes to disk, execution stays with whoever owns the session.

dsh-session-inbox README · Message format：One JSON object per line, newline-terminated. `to` must equal the file name without `.jsonl`.

```json
{"id":"<uuid>","ts":"<ISO-8601>","from":"<who>","to":"<sessionId>","text":"<body>"}
```

dsh-session-inbox README · Behaviour：| Situation | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| target live and idle | message is injected, cursor advances |
| target running | message stays in the file, no interruption |
| target not live | message stays in the file until that session exists |
| malformed line | skipped permanently so it cannot block the queue |
| multiple messages | injected one turn at a time |

The cursor lives in `~/.dsh/inbox/.state/` and only ever moves forward, so a second host cannot
rewind it and replay messages.

dsh-session-inbox README · Limits：- **No push into a session you do not own.** This plugin only serves sessions inside the DSH host
  that mounted it. It cannot reach another product's session.
- **`from` is self-declared.** Any process that can write the inbox can claim any sender. Never use
  it for authorization.
- **Delivery is not acknowledgement.** A queued message proves nothing about whether the model read
  it; agree on an id-and-echo convention if you need confirmation.

dsh-session-inbox README · Compatibility：`engines.dsh` is a floor (`>=0.1.7-0`) with no upper bound. The plugin imports nothing from the DSH
packages beyond what the host injects (`agents`), so it does not pin a harness version.
